${\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
after.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-2,-1],$ the line segment for $x\in [-1,1),$ and the line segment for $x\in [1,3].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,-1].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a square, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & ={s}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-2+4 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph consists of $2$ parts: the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [-4,-2]$ and the line segment for $x\in (-2,1].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-2].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot (1)^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-2,1].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+1)\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi +9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
